content.title: Startle-to-Truce Encounter
content.summary: Build a clear relationship reversal: a technical observer discovers a calm subject, one non-lethal panic response raises the risk, the subject approaches a transparent boundary and takes control of the distance, then sustained eye contact and a small, hesitant de-escalation gesture lower the threat.

quick_start.input_format: Calm subject + technical observer + transparent boundary + one non-lethal panic response + distance reversal + visible de-escalation gesture
quick_start.recommended_input: A curious deep-sea creature notices a research submersible, one defensive flash startles the pilot, then the creature matches the window's movement, approaches calmly, and ends with a small gesture that the pilot can clearly see.
required_anchors: A readable calm baseline must exist before escalation
The subject and the observer have independent perspectives with different information
Use only one readable, non-lethal panic or defensive reaction
Use coaxiality, matching speed, or the same frame to prove distance and initiative reversal
The final de-escalation gesture must be visible to the other party and held long enough to read; do not invent reciprocal acceptance
usage_steps: Replace the example subject, setting and surface details with an original concept.
Keep every required anchor and Creative DNA invariant causally visible.
Choose the MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 prompt and fill only the declared variable slots.
Check duration, event order, camera continuity, sound and anti-copy constraints before generation.
applicable_scope: Short encounters that move from calm observation through one readable mistake to a visible, uncertain de-escalation.
Original 4–15 second concepts that can preserve every required anchor.
MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 projects that need a reusable causal video structure.
not_suitable_for: Requests that copy the source identity, setting, props, dialogue or shot order.
Concepts that cannot show all required anchors inside the target duration.
Long-form exposition or unrelated multi-location stories without a compact causal chain.

creative_dna.mechanism: A calm subject begins at a readable distance from a technical observer. Their separate viewpoints establish an information gap, and one non-lethal panic response raises the risk. The subject then approaches a transparent boundary and takes control of the distance; sustained eye contact and one small de-escalation gesture reduce the threat without claiming that both sides have fully reconciled.
applicable_scope: Contrasting encounters between fantasy or natural subjects and technological observers or research equipment
Precise eye contact on both sides of the cockpit, submarine, observation window, greenhouse glass, or transparent barrier
Misjudgment, startle, temptation, and non-verbal reconciliation within 4–15 seconds
The reference image only locks a single character's identity; scenes and actions must be original multi-modal generation.
not_suitable_for: Content that includes complete war, multiplayer tactics, continuous explosions, or complex weapon logic
Content that uses injury, gore, or real-life assault as a necessary selling point
Overloaded storyboards that leave no time to read the final gaze and gesture
Shot-by-shot recreations of sample characters, props, vehicles, landscapes, or staging
usage_steps: Identify the calm subject, technical observer, initial distance, transparent boundaries, and final relationship status
Assign a unique identity, costume, scene, action, or voice responsibility to each input material
First, write the causal chain of calm baseline—observer’s perspective—an escalation—distance reversal—gesture de-escalation.
Compile according to H3 and Seedance native syntax respectively, without copying model fields
Check identity, vehicle, bounds, speed, screen orientation, gaze, gesture, and duration closures
invariants: A readable calm baseline must exist before escalation
The subject and the observer have independent perspectives with different information
Use only one readable, non-lethal panic or defensive reaction
Use coaxiality, matching speed, or the same frame to prove distance and initiative reversal
The final de-escalation gesture must be visible to the other party and held long enough to read; reciprocal acceptance may be shown only when explicitly established
quality_repairs: Prioritize four to five causal segments in 12–15 seconds, and delete uncompleted weapon and pursuit stacks
Name effects according to visible launch structure and direction; do not write unknown light tracks as guided missiles
Closeness occurs before the final quarter, allowing time for surprise and reconciliation
Eye height, screen direction, reflection, and relative speed are locked on both sides of the glass
Do not exaggerate a unilateral wave to mean that both parties have accepted reconciliation.
anti_copy_exclusions: Do not copy samples of fantasy women, hair accessories, fruits, flying swords, military fighter planes, or floating mountain landscapes
Do not copy the original light beam, interference flame composition, cockpit shape, or specific window placement.
Change at least eight of the following simultaneously: subject, observer, environment, boundary, motion physics, escalation device, camera treatment, color, sound, and ending behavior.

review.method: canonical-source offline English editorial pass with terminology and stable-token validation; title naming editorial pass
